title: Why do cats knead? Meet the tiny biscuit maker
description: Why do cats knead blankets and laps? The habit starts during kittenhood, but the reason adult cats keep making biscuits is less certain.

cover.alt: A tabby cat presses its front paws into a cream knitted blanket on a sofa

sources.name: Cats Protection — Why do cats knead?

sections.title: A bakery with no bread
sections.html:
Cats knead by pressing their front paws into something soft, one after the other. The habit begins when kittens feed from their mother. Those little pushes help stimulate milk flow.

Years later, the same movement can appear on your favourite blanket. People call it “making biscuits”, although the cat has supplied neither flour nor a washing-up plan.

sections.title: Why do grown-up cats still do it?
sections.html:
This is where the answer becomes less certain. Cats Protection explains that we do not know exactly why some cats keep kneading as adults.

One possibility is that the action feels comforting because of its early association with feeding. Another is that a soft texture triggers an ingrained response. These are explanations to consider, rather than thoughts we can read from a cat’s face.

sections.title: Why your blanket gets the treatment
sections.html:
A fleecy throw offers a soft surface for those repeated paw movements. Some cats choose a lap instead, turning a quiet evening into a rather pointy massage.

Kneading can go along with the familiar rumble of purring, which also has more than one meaning. Neither behaviour gives us a perfect translation of “cat”.

sections.title: A small mystery on the sofa
sections.html:
The kitten connection is clear; the adult explanation remains open. That makes the behaviour more interesting than a simple “your cat is happy” label.

For another domestic puzzle, discover why an empty box can beat an expensive cat bed. Apparently, interior design has different rules when you have whiskers.
